state:
Goal `core-zip`: `Core\Zip::entries` and `Core\Zip::read` are complete (`bun nv proofs --id 'Core\Zip::read'` owes nothing once its perf figure is recorded, which this session did for both). `Core\Zip` has its class card.
The attack on `read` found a panic: `frame` added a zip64 compressed size to the entry's start unchecked, so a claim near `u64::MAX` overflowed. The sum is now checked, pinned by `tests/conformance/core/zip-refuses-an-entry-whose-zip64-size-runs-past-the-address-space.nvst` and by the Rust test `the_member_reads_one_entry_under_a_bound_held_on_both_sides`.
`extract` still owes about, examples, hostile, perf and a Rust test with a `covers:` marker. Its `.nvst` cases already exist. It is the last thing `dossier-core-zip` is red on.

next.title: feature proofs for the rest of `Core\Zip`

items.text: **`Core\Zip::extract`** — owes about, examples, hostile, perf, a Rust `// covers:` test (`rule:testing/feature-proofs`). Registry row `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/zip.rs:167`, member body `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/zip.rs:1042`, placement `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/zip.rs:787`. Drive the member the way `read_from` does at `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/zip.rs:1335`, with a destination under a scratch directory the test removes. Every example and the attack need an `fs.write` and `fs.read` grant for the destination; how an example is granted one is not checked yet (see `docs/examples/README.md` and the playbook bullet on `--SKIPIF--` and `[[app]]` grants). The attack should target the across-the-archive half of the bound (many entries each under `maxBytes`, whose total is over), a destination that already holds a file with an entry's name, and a deep folder chain. After it lands, run `bun nv proofs --record-perf --group 'Core\Zip'`, because a change to `zip.rs` makes every member's figure stale.

backlog: `Core\Zip::read` allocates about 77 KB per call for a 244-byte entry (`docs/perf/members.ndjson`): each call builds a fresh deflate decoder and its window. Reusing the state is a latency question, not a bug — owner `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/zip.rs` module doc if it is ever taken.

`read` walks the whole central directory on every call, so reading every entry of an archive with many entries is quadratic in the entry count. Not a hang at the sizes the attacks use; worth a `# Known gaps` line if a proof ever measures it.
